dish: pho bo with bone-in short rib
w: Little Saigon's benchmark for Northern-style pho, its golden bone-marrow broth simmered nearly a day; get the pho bo dac biet or splurge on the one-pound bone-in short rib. SF Chronicle calls it a 'pho sensation' and Eater singles out its amply-portioned bowls and char-grilled pork rolls.
sources: SF Chronicle called Pho Ha Noi a 'pho sensation' (Bay Area pho coverage)
Eater praised its 'generous, amply-portioned servings' and char-grilled pork rolls

w: A family-run shrine to poultry on Story Road whose pho ga is built on a delicate broth and free-range, local chicken. The Infatuation notes it is nearly always packed, so go for a late lunch or dinner.

address: 3005 Silver Creek Rd, Ste 190, San Jose, CA 95121
w: East San Jose's Central-Vietnamese standout, where the spicy lemongrass bun bo Hue is as satisfying as its next-level banh beo and banh bot loc rice cakes at about $6 a plate. An ever-revolving line at the door tells you it leaves competitors in the dust.

address: 1020 Story Rd, Ste C, San Jose, CA 95122
w: The Infatuation calls this takeout counter the best lunch deal in San Jose: small banh mi for $4, large for $8. Get the grilled pork banh mi, punchy strips of pork and lightly pickled julienned vegetables in a crackly-yet-fluffy baguette.

address: 909 Story Rd, Unit 100, San Jose, CA 95122
w: Little Saigon's broken-rice institution, routinely called one of the best com tam in the country; the sampler stacks grilled pork chop, bi, shrimp cake and steamed egg cake over fractured rice with nuoc cham. (A second Senter Rd location has closed; the Story Rd flagship is open.)
Tucked in Little Saigon's Lion Plaza food court and worth getting lost for, per The Infatuation, for its sizzling pate-topped bo ne, a cast-iron plate of steak and eggs mopped up with baguette.

A plant-based Vietnamese spot in the Little Saigon shopping plaza drawing in-the-know locals and monks from the nearby monastery, with dishes like caramelized faux-fish claypot and sweet-and-sour hot pot in a small sunlit room.

address: 740 Story Rd, Ste 3, San Jose, CA 95122
w: A tiny family counter that does little but bun bo Hue and pho, its lemongrass-and-chili beef broth made from scratch and widely considered among the most famous bowls in San Jose. (The former Tully Rd location has closed; the Story Rd shop is open.)

address: 3005 Silver Creek Rd, Ste 176, San Jose, CA 95121
w: An East San Jose specialist whose namesake banh xeo arrives crispy-yet-chewy and stuffed with shrimp, pork and bean sprouts, torn into lettuce with herbs and nuoc cham.

address: 1818 Tully Rd, Ste 150, San Jose, CA 95122
w: The go-to in Little Saigon for bo 7 mon, the celebratory seven-courses-of-beef feast where the animal comes boiled, grilled, wrapped, minced and souped in sequence, ending in chao bo.

dish: nem nuong (grilled pork) vermicelli and rolls
address: 919 Story Rd, Ste 1100, San Jose, CA 95122
w: A Little Saigon specialist for Nha Trang-style nem nuong, springy grilled pork sausage served over bun vermicelli or rolled at the table with rice paper, herbs and a sweet dipping sauce. (An older 1111 Story Rd location has closed; the 919 Story Rd shop is open.)
